item.title: Joburg to blacklist developers after deadly Ormonde building collapse
item.description: A preventable oversight failure led to nine deaths in Ormonde in the south of Johannesburg, the city said as it announced the crackdown on unlawful developments

item.title: SANDF deployment to back police set to start on 31 March
item.description: National police commissioner Fannie Masemola said the army would play a supporting role to the South African Police Service

item.title: How finance can help build more integrated African supply chains
item.description: Regional trade becomes expensive to finance when too much of the transaction sits in separate systems that do not talk to each other

item.title: DRC crisis: Can Africans stand up to Western nations’ perpetuation of the tragic status quo?
item.description: When Congo’s President, Felix Tshisekedi, squeezes his corpulent bulk into designer clothing, accessorised with expensive watches that would feed thousands of his immiserated citizens for years and climbs into a flying palace to shuttle around the world to weep crocodile tears and move the powerful to pity his long-suffering people, it is a diversionary dance in step with his Western audience

item.title: If customary law marriage comes first, no civil marriage allowed later
item.description: Following this judgment, it’s more important than ever that anyone getting married, whether in a traditional ceremony, at the magistrate’s court or in church, should consult an attorney to help explain the options and draft a legally binding agreement that will suit the couple’s particular circumstances

item.title: Crime is increasingly detected online but policing remains offline
item.description: Being digitally present is a form of accountability: it signals that the station is not hiding behind central bureaucracy when communities are scared. It also enhances investigative capacity, as communities already share leads online, including images, videos, vehicle descriptions and patterns of movement

item.title: Stability is not the destination. It is the foundation.
item.description: Fiscal discipline, reform momentum and the role of private capital South Africa’s 2026 Budget arrives at a moment defined by both volatility and cautious optimism. National Treasury has projected that the country’s debt to GDP ratio has reached its peak. A primary surplus has been restored and fiscal consolidation has held despite multiple external shocks […]

item.title: Modernising mining: Cybersecurity must be central, not optional
item.description: At the 2026 Mining Indaba in Cape Town, the emphasis was on digitalisation and technological advancement of the industry. However, the industry recognises that cybersecurity can no longer continue to remain the unaddressed elephant in the room

item.title: Leveraging AI to achieve peace, justice, good governance
item.description: Corruption undermines public trust and hinders social and economic development. AI can combat corruption by increasing transparency, identifying suspicious activities and monitoring financial transactions for illicit practices

item.title: Malawi’s media ‘crisis’ is bigger than the newsroom
item.description: A blistering courtroom critique of journalists reveals not just professional failings but the deeper economic and institutional fragility undermining democratic accountability in Malawi
